key_insight: This paper introduces an open-source hardware-software toolkit that automates RHEED control and analysis, making agentic thin-film synthesis more accessible to both operators and AI systems.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the barrier to closed-loop materials synthesis by providing programmable electron-optics control, automated alignment, and interfaces that can be driven by software agents.
method: Programmable RHEED electron-optics control on a pulsed laser deposition system
Automated beam alignment, rocking-curve acquisition, and training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment
Shared GUI/API workflow with an MCP server and extensible adapters for new analysis or simulation methods
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstrated PLD-based implementation with an agent-driven example showing natural-language requests can select, configure, and execute quantitative analyses.
watch_item: Performance depends on robust integration with specific hardware setups and community-maintained adapters, so portability and reliability across different RHEED systems may require careful validation.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
